Query a zutable with SQL's clauses

Source: R/bracket.R
zutable-bracket.Rd

The bracket takes SQL's clauses as named arguments over bare column names: where, select, by, having, order, limit and distinct, run in SQL's logical order whatever order they are written in. The first two positions are where and select, as in data.table: x[px > 0, .(id, notional = px * qty)]. A bracket always returns a table, and its schema is known, and every type error raised, before any data is read.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zutable'
`[`(
  x,
  i,
  j,
  by,
  ...,
  where,
  select,
  update,
  having,
  order,
  limit,
  distinct = FALSE,
  drop = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A zutable.

i, where

Rows to keep: a condition (or, as a value form, an integer or logical vector).

j, select

Columns of the result: .(...) (or, as a value form, a character, integer or logical vector).

by

Groups: a column, .(a, b), .(name = expression) or a character vector of column names. NA is a group, and groups come in order of first appearance, by columns first in the result.

...

Not used.

update

An update: col := value or a block of them; see zutable-update.

having

A condition on the groups, naming result columns or aggregating input ones.

order

Sort keys.

limit

A row count.

distinct

TRUE to keep one of each distinct result row.

drop

Ignored: a bracket always returns a table.

Value

A zutable.

Details

  • select is .(...) of bare columns, name = expression, .all for every input column, and -name after .all to leave one out. A computed element needs a name.

  • order is an expression or .(...) of them, desc(x) reversing one. It may name result columns and, unless distinct, input columns. It is stable, and NA sorts last.

  • limit is a row count, applied after order.

  • With by, or an aggregate in select, the query aggregates: each element of select is an aggregate or an expression of the by keys. Without by it is a one-row summary. having filters groups.

  • over(aggregate, by = keys) computes an aggregate per partition without collapsing rows, for a select that keeps .all.

  • A name that is not a column is a variable of the caller, and enters as a constant; ..name forces the variable when a column has the same name. .col(name) is the column whose name a variable holds.

A position that mentions no column is a value form instead: an integer or logical vector selects rows and a character, integer or logical vector selects columns, as for a data frame.

Examples

x <- zutable(id = 1:4, px = c(10.5, 11, 20, 7), qty = c(100L, 50L, 10L, 200L))
x[px > 10, .(id, notional = px * qty)]
#> <zutable> 3 rows x 2 columns
#>   id      notional
#>   <int32> <float64>
#> 1 1       1050
#> 2 2       550
#> 3 3       200
x[select = .(.all, -qty), order = desc(px), limit = 2]
#> <zutable> 2 rows x 2 columns
#>   id      px
#>   <int32> <float64>
#> 1 3       20
#> 2 2       11
